title: Design a Resumable Video Generation Scheduler
prompt: Design an asynchronous video-generation service backed by a heterogeneous GPU fleet. Users submit idempotent jobs, see status/ETA, cancel work, and retrieve artifacts. Jobs may be preempted or workers may die. Cover durable state, admission control, priority and fairness, GPU compatibility, checkpoint recovery, cancellation, notifications, and observability; model training is out of scope.

response.placeholder: Separate durable job acceptance from GPU execution. State how a lease becomes invalid after worker loss.
response.reference_answer:
## Job contract
Persist an idempotency key, model/version, input artifact references, requested priority, and immutable job ID before acknowledging. Status transitions are Accepted, Queued, Leased, Running, Succeeded, Failed, or Cancelled; a result is published only after durable artifact commit.

## Scheduling and workers
Partition queues by compatible model, resolution, and GPU requirements. Apply bounded admission and tenant-aware fair scheduling rather than letting premium traffic starve old jobs. Dispatch a fenced lease with heartbeat and expiry; a worker must include the attempt/fencing token when it writes checkpoints or completion.

## Recovery and cancellation
Store periodic checkpoints in object storage. On lease expiry, reclaim from the newest committed checkpoint; late workers cannot overwrite a newer attempt. Cancellation is durable, checked between work units, and prevents result publication. Use an outbox for status notifications.

## Metrics
Track queue age by class, admission rejects, GPU compatibility misses, lease expiry, checkpoint age, resumed-job success, cancellation latency, artifact integrity, cost, and ETA calibration.

## Progressive Hints
1. A queue record is not a worker lease.
2. Checkpoints and final artifacts need attempt fencing.
3. ETA must account for queue and service time.
